name: Cumin
summary: One of the most widely used spices in the world. Warm, earthy, and faintly citrusy — present in nearly every major spice tradition from Mexico to Morocco.
description: Cumin seeds are crescent-shaped, ribbed, and yellow-brown. Whole seeds develop richer, nuttier flavour when dry-toasted before grinding. Ground cumin is a backbone spice in Mexican, Indian, North African, and Middle Eastern blends. Black cumin (kala zeera) is distinct — longer and darker, with an anise-like profile. Store whole seeds for best longevity; ground cumin loses its vibrancy quickly.
